messages:
alex: customer reports login loop + 400 on OAuth callback for both GitHub and Google. state param they sent is 'abc+123' but our server sees 'abc 123' and we return 400 state_mismatch
rita: ugh, classic encoding weirdness. do we have any reverse proxy or rewrite in front of the app?
sam: customer says they run Apache mod_rewrite rules to strip /prod prefix before proxying to the app. they pasted the rule: 

RewriteEngine On
RewriteRule ^prod/(.*)$ /$1 [R=301,L]
ProxyPass / http://internal-app:8080/
ProxyPassReverse / http://internal-app:8080/

sam: also their callback URL is https://app.customer.io/prod/oauth/callback
rita: ok. two things that bite: mod_rewrite + querystring handling and how Apache may decode plus signs into spaces when the qs is processed. can you repro locally with their exact rule?
eng-oncall: repro steps i used: 
1) start a tiny echo server expecting state param exactly 'abc+123'
2) hit curl -v "https://app.customer.io/prod/oauth/callback?state=abc+123&code=xyz"
observed on backend: state=abc 123 (space)
support-bot: log snippet from customer (sanitized): 
[access] GET /prod/oauth/callback?state=abc+123&code=xyz 302 -> /internal/callback.php 200
[srv] PHP $_GET['state'] => "abc 123"

alex: ok that explains the mismatch. GitHub/Google send + as literal '+' in their redirect, but when proxy/rewrite chain decodes the qs incorrectly we end up comparing wrong string.
rita: quick mitigation: ask customer to preserve the raw querystring through Apache rewrite. a common fix is to use the [QSA,B] flags on RewriteRule or avoid rewriting the path part that triggers a qs rebuild. e.g.,

RewriteRule ^prod/(.*)$ /$1 [R=301,L,QSA,B]

Note: B (escape backreferences) will percent-encode characters in backreferences so + stays %2B rather than becoming space

sam: alternative minimal change: proxy the callback path directly (no rewrite) and let ProxyPass handle it. or ensure the redirect to internal doesn't re-interpret the querystring.
eng-oncall: i'll prepare a short repro PR for our app to log raw REQUEST_URI and raw query bytes so we can confirm the upstream fix.
rita: please also ask the customer to test by encoding the state explicitly: state=abc%2B123 and see if that works as a short-term workaround.
alex: customer tried state=abc%2B123 and said it worked. they prefer a platform-side fix though since they have many integrations.
sam: pulled together suggested change and commands to test: 

# test curl that reproduces the bad case
curl -v "https://app.customer.io/prod/oauth/callback?state=abc+123&code=xyz"

# test curl encoded
curl -v "https://app.customer.io/prod/oauth/callback?state=abc%2B123&code=xyz"

eng-oncall: deployed a logging patch to staging to record raw REQUEST_URI, backend shows %2B in encoded test and space in unencoded test. forwarding the logs to customer.
support-bot: ticket updated: workaround documented, suggested Apache config patch with QSA,B flags, ask them to confirm SSL terminate/proxy layers are not re-decoding qs.
alex: customer applied the RewriteRule change with [QSA,B] and confirmed OAuth flows are green for both GitHub and Google, no more state_mismatch. closing as resolved after they verify for 24h :thumbsup:
rita: added a KB note: "OAuth callback: Apache mod_rewrite may convert '+' to space — use B flag or preserve raw querystring". linking to this thread + sample rules.
eng-oncall: marking follow-up to add better diagnostics into our callback handler: log raw_uri + hex of qs so future ones are faster to diagnose.
sam: thanks team, glad that was a simple fix.
alex: closing thread.
